question: Should the standard Chrome/Web Store build intentionally drop debugger-backed automation and move that capability to the separate automation build for existing users?
rationale: This is a security and Web Store permission boundary improvement, but it changes an existing automation capability for standard-build users and cannot be settled by tests alone.

options.title: Accept the split
options.body: Ship the standard build without debugger access and require users who need native input or the debugger tool to use the explicit automation build.

options.title: Clarify distribution first
options.body: Keep the PR open until the automation build's packaging and upgrade path are documented enough that users and release steps cannot confuse it with the Web Store build.

options.title: Preserve current capability
options.body: Do not merge this boundary change and keep debugger-backed automation in the standard Chrome build despite the broader install-time permission.

recommendation.title: Accept the split
recommendation.body: Ship the standard build without debugger access and require users who need native input or the debugger tool to use the explicit automation build.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the PR and is the only clear recent history owner for the affected extension permission and automation paths.
